{"file_path":"SPEC.md","content":"# Pack spec

## Goal template

The primary target is a clock period in ns, named on the Run and pushed one step at a time.

Shaped by `over-constrain-and-read-the-violation.md`: the target is asked one step tighter than the period believed possible, so that what comes back is a violation with a size rather than a pass with none.

## Constraints

One constraint: the setup slack the verification report states, in ns, against the period the run asked for. It is checked, not assumed, and the options it was measured under are stated beside it.

Shaped by `assert-the-checker-options.md`: a constraint met under options nobody declared is a constraint met for the wrong reason.

## Run contract

Inputs: where the flow lies, which design is run, and where campaign workspaces are made.
Outputs: the verification report of each generation, read into typed values.
Wrappers: the flow's own build tool, and nothing else.
Tools: one per stage of the flow, each stating its variables on the command line.

Shaped by `what-a-golden-flow-is.md`: the flow is read where it lies and copied into a campaign workspace, never into this pack.

## Semantics

- `setupSlackNs` — ns — how far the worst path is from meeting the period the run asked for. Negative is a violation.
- `askedPeriodNs` — ns — the period that generation asked for.

Shaped by `over-constrain-and-read-the-violation.md`: both values are needed, because the achievable period is the one read off the other.

## Judge rules

A generation continues when the report was produced under the declared options and both values were read; it is blocked when either is missing.

Shaped by `assert-the-checker-options.md`: the verdict cites the options as well as the numbers.

## Choosers

One chooser: on a violation, the next period is the period asked plus the size of the violation; on a met constraint, the next period is one step tighter.

Shaped by `over-constrain-and-read-the-violation.md`, which is the move itself.

## Endings

Goal met; converged, when two generations agree on the achievable period; and one this pack declares in its own words — the flow refusing to run at all, which is an ending and not a failure to explain.

Shaped by `end-honestly-in-more-than-one-way.md`: none of the three is a generation limit.

## Workshops

None. Nothing in this pack is written by the AI at run time: every command line a generation runs
is one of the tool scripts the next stage writes, and every number it reads is read by a declared
reader. A workshop here would be a place for code nobody asked for.

Shaped by `one-checker-per-session.md`: the only reason this pack would need one is to drive a
second checker, and it drives one.

## Knowledge

The pack's own knowledge files to write, by name and purpose:

- `push-method.md` — why this pack pushes the period the way it does, and where the two values it
  reads live in the report, for a Model moment to read.

Shaped by `attribute-by-database-relation.md`, which is why that file tells nobody to match a name
in a file when a tool's own database holds the relation.
"}

block.text: SPEC.md is written beside the record: the nine sections, each in this pack's own words and each naming the knowledge file that shaped it.
